dedupe_keys.name: machine learning for healthcare accessibility developing a vulnerability index for u s pharmacy deserts data and code

description: Nathan Umberger and colleagues publish county-level data and a Jupyter analysis notebook for a pharmacy-accessibility index. Zenodo archives a CC BY 4.0 release; the linked repository README describes 735 counties in Pennsylvania, Ohio, California, Texas, Indiana, Kentucky and Montana. Predictors draw on 2024 County Health Rankings, while the pharmacy-desert labels use an earlier GoodRx classification. The notebook compares several classifiers, calculates a Pharmacy Desert Index and exports predicted county probabilities. These data can help calibrate healthcare-service accessibility or test equity effects of pharmacy-location scenarios. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this seven-state dataset. A limitation is that county aggregation masks within-county travel barriers, and 2021 outcome labels do not describe current pharmacy closures. The public release is study-specific, not a nationwide live service inventory. No archive was downloaded, and counts, model scores and exported index values were not reproduced.
